title: Low-degree learner run distribution
statement: For natural numbers $n$, $\ell$, and $m$, and a Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, running the low-degree polynomial learner with target $f$ has the same probability law as drawing a uniformly random sequence $(x_i)_{i=1}^m$ from $\{−1,1\}^n$, returning the learner’s output on the labeled samples $(x_i,f(x_i))$, and assigning cost $(m,0,m+W)$, where $W$ is the learner’s charged work on those samples.
